title: Compatible K-flat representatives of a semilinear coefficient tower
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$, and a scheme $T$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $B_n=(O/\ell^n)_T$ for $n\geq1$, and let $\operatorname{Tow}(T,O)$ be the abelian category of semilinear coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Let $C_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,O))$, with exact derived evaluations $C_n\in D(B_n)$ and transitions $t_n:C_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{n+1}\to B_n}C_n$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. There exist complexes $Q_n$ of $B_n$-modules, K-flat with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], semilinear chain maps $q_n:Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$, and isomorphisms $e_n:Q_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n$ in $D(B_n)$ such that $\operatorname{Res}(e_n)\circ Q(q_n)=t_n\circ e_{n+1}$ in $D(B_{n+1})$; here $Q$ denotes localization and the restriction is along $B_{n+1}\to B_n$. The longer chain transitions are composites and represent all the original composite transitions.

After restricting scalars to $R$, this compatible family lifts to an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$ between the strict $R$-tower $Q_\bullet$ and the levelwise restriction of $C_\bullet$. Its evaluations are the specified $e_n$; applying total derived inverse limit respects every evaluation projection [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Only existence of such a lift is asserted. For every $1\leq m\leq n$, the chain map $Q_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m\to Q_m$, $x\otimes b\mapsto bq_{n,m}(x)$, represents, via the $e_n$ and K-flat change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the original canonical reduction map $C_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m\to C_m$ in $D(B_m)$.

proof.text: Represent C by a cochain complex M using essential surjectivity of localization. Transport M through D.equivalence and apply strictRingSystem_kFlatResolution once. Transport the resulting complex and augmentation back through the cochain equivalence. Exactness preserves the quasi-isomorphism. The counit evaluation isomorphisms transport the componentwise K-flatness and flat terms. Localizing the augmentation and composing with Q(M) ≅ C gives a.

proof.text: For each ordered pair, the ordinary reduction is the adjunction transpose of the strict chain transition by ordinaryReduction_eq. This identity holds degreewise and therefore for cochain maps. The normalized scalar-model transpose formula identifies its localized derived adjunct. Naturality of the original reduction at a, together with reduction_rep and the exact-evaluation factor isomorphisms, gives the reduction square. The adjunction naturality square then gives the strict transition equation. The scalar-model pure-tensor formula gives c ⊗ x ↦ c q(x). The K-flat computation field makes the counit invertible at every evaluated representative.

proof.text: The completed projections form a cone: after forgetting commutativity this is limit.w, using coefficientRings_eq. Restrict each level to the completed ring, retaining the underlying transition map; the cone equation proves its linearity. Identity, composition and naturality follow sectionwise from the strict-system laws. The resulting functor commutes definitionally with evaluation. Exactness follows componentwise from exact restriction. Apply its derived functor to a, with the canonical factor isomorphism. Naturality of the derived comparison between the two evaluation composites gives the specified evaluation equation, after cancelling the factor isomorphisms. The final equation for every supplied derived-limit projection is its naturality at the resulting lift.

I checked by hand the evaluation adjunction (right Kan extension: F at levels j>=n, terminal below), the squares Res(e_n)Q(q_n)=t_n e_{n+1}, exactness of U and naturality of the R lim triangle for the projections. Edge cases checked: empty T, n=1, m=n (unitor), nonflat Z/l^2->Z/l, unbounded C. No duplicate among the def-coef-*/lem-coef-* sequence-site nodes and no cycle. lean.note: The predicate packages precisely the model conclusions, using the recorded tower category, flat-term K-flat predicate, normalized reductions and actual completed coefficient projections. One complex of towers supplies all coherent chain transitions. No boundedness, tower normalization, quotient flatness or universe equality is assumed. The normalized scalar data and pure tensors use def-weil-pbc-system-scalar-model; derived localizations use HasDerivedCategory.standard from def-weil-abstract-derived-category, not the scalar-model existence theorem. The pure-tensor clause is factored through systemTensorSectionFormula, the identical sectionwise equality on generic sheaf modules, to avoid expensive specialized scalar-action conversion. No mathematical condition changes.
